- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% if price is falling sharply.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising, or rises after falling), model often fails to correct; apply “mean reversion bias” — if 3-day moving avg deviates > 3% from 10-day avg, adjust forecast toward that avg.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 5 values by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +1.00, -0.50, +1.00), model may misread momentum; use “sentiment cycle” rule — if sentiment flips within 5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
